reviews.text: A taut story, elegant direction, and a rich, nuanced performance from Maika Monroe make Watcher a tense and unforgettable watch. From the score to the production design, every aspect of the film is infused with a sense of restrained beauty.
reviews.author: Brian Bisesi

reviews.text: Perfectly capturing what it’s like to be adrift in an unfamiliar place
reviews.author: Marya E. Gates

reviews.text: The film maintains such a naturalistic tone that the few scares doled out throughout are effective and the minimal bloodshed is subtle. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Tomás Andrés Guerrero

reviews.text: sustained package that delivers on so many fronts that what could have so easily been a formulaic slasher, genuinely pushes the boundaries of its genre, toying with an unusual bleakness that will keep audiences guessing until the end.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: Watcher is a slow burn that is highly reminiscent of Old Hollywood, cat-and-mouse thrillers.
reviews.author: Paul Lê

reviews.text: Others have noted allusions to titles as varied as Halloween and Rosemary’s Baby, and I would add Repulsion to the list. Watcher is more modest than these movies, but the comparisons indicate that viewers should do well to keep track of Okuno’s career...
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: Simple and effective -- at least to a certain point... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Rosado

reviews.text: The film asks us to endure as it continues to test our ability to trust the word of a character who is all apathy and fragility until the last few minutes. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Santiago Alverú

reviews.text: By no means is the baseline plot original but it’s the carefully crafted scenes and quiet sense of menace that hangs in the air that make Watcher a fresh horror thriller.
reviews.author: Katie Hogan

reviews.text: WATCHER is a gorgeous film of delicate tension. It’s an icy and elegant study of the constant state of fear that many women live in every day.
reviews.author: Dolores Quintana

reviews.text: The routine plot attempts to pull a few minor twists and turns, but it ultimately plays out exactly how you’d expect it to, leaving little to watch for in Watcher.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Watcher is a taut, tense and immensely watchable thriller. Plus that last shot is one for the ages.
reviews.author: Dallas King

reviews.text: Okuno's direction and Monroe's performance, together, create a simmering anxiety that never really relents.
reviews.author: Anna Bogutskaya

reviews.text: It's a shame there's not much more to the film, but it definitely gets our hearts pumping a bit faster.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Okuno’s Watcher is smart, engaging and intelligent, and it’s especially refreshing to see this sort of mid-budget, grown-up genre film getting a proper theatrical release.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: There are few genuine surprises, perhaps, but there are distinctive elements here which set the film apart, not least the way lack of fluency in a language creates a sense of siege.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: Watcher feels like a throwback to slower-paced psychological thrillers. It's deserving of your attention.
reviews.author: Bren Murphy

reviews.text: A generic, unnecessary and forgettable thriller that barely stands out for the charm of its protagonist. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Jose Cruz

reviews.text: In an impressively assured cinematic debut, writer-director Chloe Okuno builds the suspense splendidly...
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Okuno uses all the tools at the film-maker’s disposal to make us share Julia’s creeping sense of dread.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: Watcher’s effectiveness lies in its simplicity and this film reflects on some of the most omnipresent of human worries, with a concentrated quality that makes it an undeniably chilling and relatable affair.
reviews.author: Jack Bottomley

reviews.text: Even as it starts embracing some of the genre tropes familiar from classics such as Repulsion and Rosemary’s Baby, it offers a fresh take on how those ideas sit in the current moment and singles Akuno out as a filmmaker to watch.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: A very solidly engineered Hitchcockian throwback.
reviews.author: Mike McCahill

reviews.text: Even though it could be classified as a psychological and mystery thriller, almost all directorial decisions by Okuno move the film towards unrestrained horror... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: Not to put too fine a point on it, but if the cops are taking the word of a dude who looks like *Burn Gorman* over you, something else has to be going on.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Watcher doesn’t add anything new to the “stalker” subgenre, but it still satisfies thanks to a sustained sense of suspense throughout and Maika Monroe’s powerful lead performance.
reviews.author: Zoë Rose Bryant

reviews.text: It’s a slow burn with some decent suspense.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: The plot is more or less a way into Okuno’s thoughts about a woman being infantilized, dismissed, and not believed when she raises a red flag.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Watcher is moody, tense, and surprisingly effective as a slow-burn horror indie.
reviews.author: Taylor Antrim

reviews.text: And elegant thriller and feminist cautionary tale. 'Watcher' (and there is some question as to who is the watcher and who is being watched) is genuinely frightening.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: More of a psychological thriller than hardcore horror, more character study than a serial killer portrait, Watcher stands out for its rigorous feminine/ist point of view... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: a polished and engaging thriller that is assembled from a host of familiar bits and pieces from superior films, but still works in its own right
reviews.author: James Kendrick

reviews.text: The director, avoiding complicating what is simple, makes it straightforward, with no frivolous scares.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Director Chloe Okuno, who wrote the story for the screen based on Zack Ford’s screenplay, gives a stylish, contemporary female spin on a classic old-school thriller, and it gets under your skin with her methodical approach.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Doesn't offer much in the way of surprises but Okuno's masterful, claustrophobic direction and Monroe's empathetic lead performance make Watcher a must-watch (sorry).
reviews.author: Trace Thurman

reviews.text: Watcher is a mesmerizing, understated, slow-burn thriller with long stares and poky elevators and a firm grip on both ends of the gradual taffy-pull of suspense.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Chloe Okuno’s feature debut is a moody psychological thriller that feels fresh despite a wash-rinse-and-repeat narrative.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: Writer-director Chloe Okuno overdelivers on the promise of her movie's title but, in doing so, underwhelms in creating suspense.
reviews.author: Tara McNamara

reviews.text: It grabs you along the way.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: The director has the ability to suck the air right out of the room with the way she mounts tension and suspense.
reviews.author: Nicolás Delgadillo

reviews.text: Though the "thriller" aspects of it are perhaps a bit too routine (and, in some cases, downright silly), the potent, unsettling way in which it gets under Julia's skin makes Watcher is a success.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: The filmmaker has a powerful partner in Monroe, who quietly provides insight into Julia’s emotions and thought processes.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: This film is like a heaping plate of French fries, crispy and dripping with salt. We know it's essentially worthless, but it tastes so delicious.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Maika Monroe's best role to date in another Hitchcockian variation about voyeurism and the male gaze that is often intimate and creepy. Wish it had a stronger, more plausible conclusion but the journey is still worth investing in.
reviews.author: Jim Laczkowski

reviews.text: Through this lens, through this empowered performance, familiar material feels very different.
reviews.author: Jennie Kermode

reviews.text: “Watcher” is a spellbinding throwback to the thrillers of yesterday that dares you to look away.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: It's content to play with common fears and never becomes a fully satisfying chiller.
reviews.author: Matthew St. Clair

reviews.text: Good movie -- solid as a rock!
reviews.author: Tim Cogshell

reviews.text: This is all potentially fodder for a pulp movie, but instead it was extremely well-directed, very evocative, and more like a psychological thriller.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Watcher exposes the subtle erosion and self-delusion that's part and parcel to gaslighting someone.
reviews.author: Ro Moore

reviews.text: Watcher showcases writer/director Chloe Okuno as an auteur poised in her singular vision.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: One of the best horror movies of recent years
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: If you’re patient, the film will take you on one heck of a satisfying ride that’s kept comfortably above water by strong performances from Maika Monroe and Burn Gorman.
reviews.author: Amelia Emberwing

reviews.text: With Watcher, Okuno and Monroe take us on a rollercoaster of emotions. Atmospheric, taut, and engaging, Okuno’s assured direction is evident in every frame.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: Watcher never pretends to reinvent the wheel, and that’s a good thing. When everyone can bring their A+ game, instead of trying to work in non-sensical twists and turns, it allows a film to succeed where others fail.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: A moody, slow-simmering piece of work that proves that a solid chiller can still be made from modest materials.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: ‘Watcher’ Dares You To Look Away
reviews.author: Joey Moser

reviews.text: (Maika) Monroe is such an underrated talent, skilled at conveying tense, palpable emotions in films like these.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Theme never hijacks tension in Watcher, which is content to let meaning emerge organically from the familiar cat-and-mouse games of its slender genre plot.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: An atmospheric, but pedestrian thriller low on surprises, scares and intrigue.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: A different kind of voyeur/stalker film, as events are filtered through a bad marriage and the psychological questions of Julia's paranoia and motivations, which in a larger sense represents the patriarchal law enforcement system. Maika Monroe rules!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: With just a few characters, a stripped-down setting, and a somewhat familiar scenario, Okuno maximizes tension with every frame of her feature directorial debut, delivering one of the most tense movie experiences you're likely to have this year.
reviews.author: Matthew Jackson

reviews.text: You feel that anxiety attack right alongside Julia
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Okuno’s taut feature artfully reconstructs a Hitchcockian thriller around, yes, a blonde heroine in Monroe, but one with her own gaze and distinct anxieties.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: It’s ultimately more of a well-wrought genre piece than a new vision in terror...Yet its creepy unease lingers.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: A chilly and elegant thriller.
reviews.author: Sheila O'Malley

reviews.text: Watcher is an eye-opening and artful directorial debut for Chloe Okuno, who uses her deceptively simple premise to challenge those quick to doubt and dismiss female victims.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Monroe and a clever ending make it worth a look.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: It’s evident that there is a rich knowledge of cinema coursing through Okuno’s mind, as she obviously draws from films such as Peeping Tom, Rear Window, or a movie that Monroe is familiar with in It Follows.
reviews.author: Leo Brady

reviews.text: A gorgeously shot, often glacial thriller steeped in heavy-lidded style and atmosphere.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: After building tension slowly and steadily, it’s a shame this psychological thriller lacks the payoff to match its creepy setup.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: There's the usual array of red herrings, plausible explanations, and so on, and the main performers effectively sell their respective roles and related trappings to the point that you truly worry about the protagonist and her safety.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Whether you find your patience rewarded or punished by the final moments is a toss-up. The ending will get you talking, so the view is still good. But "Watcher" would benefit from a cleaner window into the borderland between imagined & irrefutable terror.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Though reminiscent of Hitchcock, Polanski and others, this white-knuckle thriller soars on strong performances and its eastern European setting.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: This beautifully crafted jewel of a throwback thriller signifies Okuno as a talent to watch, but furthermore, it pushes the viewer to question what, and who, we choose to believe and why.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: But while a few more corpses and a bit more on-screen danger might have made “Watcher” more intense, it would be counterproductive to luxuriate in cinematic violence in a film that’s all about why it’s wrong not to take stalking and violence seriously.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: While it’s overly familiar, Monroe’s strong performance is the thing that makes “Watcher” watchable.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: Monroe is fantastic in this role. Her Julia is juggling her own skepticism with that gut feeling telling her something is wrong. Okuno might be writing fiction, but this terror is very, very real.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: This isn't a movie about conspiracies or plot twists, but about a heightened version of an everyday experience for many women, and Okuno keeps it grounded even when ramping up the danger.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Okuno crafts a superior, stylish thriller, rich with nods to the 1960s and the golden era of paranoia dramas.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: It's simple but scary stuff.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The real killer in this story is the cliché.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: Okuno deftly elevates “Watcher” from a Hitchcockian homage to one of this century’s most arresting tales of female anxiety.
reviews.author: Lena Wilson

reviews.text: A cut above any number of this type of film.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: Okuno is just a fantastic filmmaker with a great eye for cinema ... that eye and talent is fully on display in her seriously disturbing feature debut.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The differences between how men and women perceive threats are always forefront in Okuno’s narrative, a (mis-)understanding gap she literalizes by relocating the American Julia to Bucharest.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: Watcher is a dark and atmospheric thriller steeped in uncertainty. The narrative uses fear as a dagger that slowly twists. Watcher will have you hooked until an utterly disappointing climax. It devolves to predictability after a superb initial set-up.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: It’s a slow-burn piece, building up its sense of dread with methodical care, all the while making a larger case against the subjugation of women and how rarely they can feel safe in any environment.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: With minimal violence, Okuno upends creepy conventions with an engrossing, meaningful take on the woman-in-jeopardy story.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: “Watcher” isn't steady and it's far from riveting, but there are moments of genre clarity and distress worth sticking around for.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Classic cinema fans will appreciate references to classic thrillers like "Charade" and "Rear Window," but more than anything, they highlight "Watcher's" own shortcomings.
reviews.author: Will Mavity

reviews.text: A mildly tense thriller that keeps its mystery just within reach. With some solid performances, it certainly makes for an enthralling watch.
reviews.author: Jordy Sirkin

reviews.text: ...the filmmaker knows how to stylishly turn the screws, her film exhibiting flashes of Hitchcockian brilliance.  Too bad about the compromised ending, but “Watcher” will creep up on you.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: This is late-night fare that will keep you rapt for 90 minutes and quickly fade from memory afterward, but leave you eager to see what Okuno does next.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: A film where a single hand wave can be as terrifying as any flashy chase scene.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: Genre fans will recognize the devices Okuno employs and suspect how they'll pay off, and the director skillfully teases those expectations... and keeps us off-balance throughout.
reviews.author: Michael Gingold

reviews.text: Voyeurism, paranoia, and the feeling of being out of one’s element underpin this tense character study.
reviews.author: Laura Bradley

reviews.text: A creepy technical exercise...ultimately undone by its clench-fisted resistance to budge from textbook tropes.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Zhang

reviews.text: Watcher succeeds more often than not when it comes to immersing viewers into a tension-filled stalker mystery. The cast members' believable performances elevate the movie's repetitive tendencies and predictable ending.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: Okuno definitely has a feel for atmosphere but the look is not enough.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Watcher establishes two acts of highly-effective slow burn that lead to an anti-climactic finale that takes no risks.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: Chloe Okuno's feature directorial debut does all it can to overcome its most glaring problem: a screenplay that does nothing new and relies heavily on dated tropes.
reviews.author: Christopher Cross

reviews.text: A thriller and drama, The Watcher captures the way women silence our inner warning bells because of gaslighting men.
reviews.author: DarkSkyLady

reviews.text: A terrific and highly effective, albeit low-grade, suspense film.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: A smart, controlled movie of pricks and gestures and tones that accumulate into a satisfying catharsis.
reviews.author: Jake Kring-Schreifels

reviews.text: The movie draws you into its 1970s-style slow burn thriller intensity with such ease and precision, you won't feel it sneaking up on you right away.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: While Watcher doesn't necessary tread new terrain, it builds genuine anxiety and tension. Okuno and Monroe put their own mark on the stalker genre, and deliver a creepy, slow-burn, psychological thriller.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: A fairly stock standard affair and follows too many familiar tropes to be something truly special.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: Watcher is a dark, smart treasure of a film, with the collaborative energy of Okuno and Monroe very much at the heart of what makes it such a compelling viewing experience.
reviews.author: Alexandra Heller-Nicholas

reviews.text: A stunning gaslighting whodunit, [with] a blood-curdling villain for the ages.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: It does justice to the genre.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Watcher is a vividly realized and expertly bone-chilling paranoid thriller.
reviews.author: Chad Collins

reviews.text: Monroe has to carry Julia's swirling emotions - loneliness, apprehension, paranoia, and anger that Francis doesn't believe her - and does so with grace and fury.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: Watcher takes these threads, these finite definers of paranoia fear and isolation, and molds them into a slow-burn thriller that doesn't always keep its finger on the pulse.
reviews.author: Kristy Strouse

reviews.text: Dripping with ice over a barely repressed inner fire, this throwback to the days of De Palma and Polanski isn't maybe up to its inspiration's high-rise standards, but it's got a sleek edge that I reveled to anyway
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: [Director Chloe Okuno's] meticulous visual storytelling lends itself well to the sense of creeping doom reinforced in almost every scene.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Watcher is a mostly standard issue thriller, albeit one elevated by its taut direction, Maika Monroe's solid lead performance, and its well-placed "believe women" context.
reviews.author: Shaun Munro

reviews.text: Okuno keeps the plot simmering for longer than some audiences may hope, but Monroe's magnetic screen presence keeps us invested and the bloody, white-knuckle conclusion is a solid payoff.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: As thrillers go, Watcher is fairly by-the-numbers, though the change in setting and the timely topics ensure there's enough to satisfy most viewers.
reviews.author: Kat Hughes

reviews.text: This is a stylish thriller from Okuno that suffers from the overall story lacking originality... But the solid performances elevate these factors.
reviews.author: Alysha Prasad

reviews.text: You'll likely work out where Watcher is heading before it gets there, but its commitment to building dread never lets up, and it will absolutely inspire you to draw all the shades in your house. Immediately.
reviews.author: Cheryl Eddy

reviews.text: It's an effort in restraint that creates a more classical slow burn that's high on technical elements but is let down by a rather pedestrian script.
reviews.author: Terry Mesnard

reviews.text: Watcher wears its influences on its sleeve with pride. A lesser filmmaker, or a film with a lesser leading lady, would just come off as derivative. That's not the case here.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Monroe, Okuno and cinematographer Benjamin Kirk Nielsen team for a superior chiller, making excellent use of Bucharest's COVID-emptied streets to evoke the still of fright.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: An old-fashioned thriller with a modern heartbeat, an announcement of Okuno as a major talent to watch.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: Monroe is good and cinematographer Benjamin Kirk Nielsen brings an eerie feeling of just barely not being able to make out certain details. The only real problem is that everything here feels familiar.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Watcher builds its thrills around some familiar elements, but sharp direction and a stellar lead performance work to keep the film a step or three ahead of its peers.
reviews.author: Rob Hunter

reviews.text: Without any aid from the script, Watcher is left to anticlimactically stumble into becoming the worst thing a horror-thriller can be: predictable.
reviews.author: Molly Adams

reviews.text: Watcher never really elevates past its stereotypical thriller roots. Okuno crafted a well-made thriller, but from the second it ends nothing follows you home.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Not a groundbreaking premise, but it's well-executed, and built.
reviews.author: Rosa Parra

reviews.text: Okuno and Ford paint a vignette of true nightmares in Watcher, and it is hard to take our eyes off of it until it reaches its final conclusion.
reviews.author: Therese Lacson

reviews.text: This is a thriller that stays stuck in first gear way too long for its own good.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Watcher gives a feminist twist to a throwback genre, but never does its topicality dilute its gripping suspense.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: The nerve-rattling movie builds to a gruesome climax. It's a first-rate thriller.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: This is a solid, well executed thriller, but it's hard not to wish that the film took more narrative risks. For fans looking for a fresh take on a 70s woman-in-danger narrative, Watcher doesn't offer any surprises.
reviews.author: Joe Lipsett

reviews.text: A film that sustains a viable ambiance of dread simply via someone looking out the window and shopping for groceries.
reviews.author: Jordan Mintzer

reviews.text: A straightforward little B-treat, Monroe's furtive glances out her Rear Window morph Watcher into a moody thriller elevated by its acting.
reviews.author: Jacob Oller

reviews.text: Did I loveWatcher? No. Did I enjoy it? Yes.
reviews.author: Norman Gidney

reviews.text: Watcher taps into a very real anxiety. It’s about not being seen. Or in this case, not being seen except by a stalker who might just be a serial killer. But [Chloe] Okuno isn't interested in reveling in that dread. She's interested in conquering it.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: With scenes suggesting too many possible explanations on the one hand, and others leaving little room for doubt, the moment-to-moment stakes feel blurred.
reviews.author: Elena Lazic

reviews.text: Thrillers are rarely scary but Watcher never misses an opportunity to put you in a panic.
reviews.author: Jonathan DeHaan

reviews.text: A thriller that both leans into the formulaic mentality of the genre whilst simultaneously hoping to combat it, Watcher (...) is a dread-filled effort that plays on the terrors of voyeurism.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: Follows the stalker thriller genre tropes fairly closely but is still suspenseful, intense & a whole lot of fun. That final shot is perfection.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Okuno's ability to create eerie unease from an uncomplicated premise impresses. It's a measured, moody psychodrama that allows Okuno to wear her influences on her sleeves, making them her own, until one satisfying finale.
reviews.author: Meagan Navarro

reviews.text: "Watcher" fails to live up to its inspirations, ending up a heavy-handed, predictable trip through genre tropes with a rather lifeless cast at its core.
reviews.author: Susannah Gruder

reviews.text: "Watcher" is actually pretty damn good. That's thanks in large part to a terrific Maika Monroe, who gets the mature, psychologically rich showcase she's fully earned with all the running and bleeding she's done heretofore as a horror heroine.
reviews.author: Jessica Kiang

reviews.text: "Watcher" might follow predictable terrain, but Maika Monroe is a solid presence and Chloe Okuno creates some creepy and skin crawling shots.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: A thriller that substitutes atmosphere for thrills.
reviews.author: Chris Evangelista

reviews.text: Beautifully shot and incredibly tense. The plot is familiar, but remains engaging. Starts to get twist heavy in the third act.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Muir

reviews.text: 'Watcher' perfects the stalker-thriller with a confident lead turn from Maika Monroe and refined, tension-wracked direction from Chloe Okuno.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

synopsis: As a serial killer stalks the city, Julia -- a young actress who just moved to town with her boyfriend -- notices a mysterious stranger watching her from across the street in this terrifying thriller.
